cards.title: Doublon-Holon Collider on 42 Qubits Validates Bethe-Ansatz Scattering Matrix
cards.why_it_matters: For anyone tracking quantum hardware progress and quantum simulation, this is a concrete milestone: a parameter-free match to an exactly solvable model on real quantum hardware.
cards.summary: On IBM's 42-qubit ibm_boston processor, researchers simulated quasiparticle scattering in the Fermi-Hubbard model using a 21-site half-filled chain. They measured doublon-holon transmission probabilities that agree with the Bethe-ansatz scattering matrix without free parameters, and inferred entanglement generation from particle-number fluctuations. A control doublon-doublon collision showed no interaction dependence, as expected for indistinguishable particles.

cards.title: Cryptographically Hidden Capabilities in LLM Weights Are Provably Unelicitable — Implications for Safety Evals
cards.why_it_matters: This directly challenges the reliability of capability evaluations used in AI safety and deployment decisions — a must-know result for anyone working on evals, red-teaming, or model auditing.
cards.summary: The authors construct backdoor attacks that embed encrypted neural networks inside host model weights, activated only by a secret trigger. Using digital lockers, hidden circuits are provably hard to elicit or interpret even with full weight access, under cryptographic assumptions. Fine-tuning, weight noising, gradient-based trigger search, and latent adversarial training all fail to surface a hidden chemical reaction prediction capability. Models are released publicly.

cards.title: LLMs vs. Humans in the Wikipedia Game: Best Models Reach Human-Level Navigation
cards.why_it_matters: If you build retrieval or agent systems that navigate large document graphs, this benchmark reveals which models succeed and where they break down across languages and domains.
cards.summary: Researchers tested sentence embedding models and LLMs on the Wikipedia Game — navigating to a target article via links — across five Wikipedia languages and five academic citation datasets built with OpenAlex. No model significantly outperformed humans, but GPT-o3 mini, GPT-4o, QwQ:32B, and DeepSeek-R1:70B achieved comparable success. Performance and rankings varied by language and topic.

cards.title: Hide and Seek (HnS): Black-Box Concept Attribution for Vision Models Without Weight Access
cards.why_it_matters: As an AI engineer working on model interpretability or vision systems, HnS extends concept-level attribution to tasks like captioning and segmentation where no prior method applies, and requires neither model weights nor labeled concept datasets.
cards.summary: HnS retrieves concept-aligned images via a vision-language model, localizes and masks the concept region, then measures attribution from output change in the black-box model — enabling local, faithful attribution. Validated on CelebA and COCO-Stuff, it outperforms existing methods on agreement with ground-truth attributions, and applies to image captioning and satellite image segmentation where prior methods fail.

cards.title: Warped Born Rule Creates Maxwell's Demon: Observation Drives Phase Transitions in Quantum Gases
cards.why_it_matters: A foundational quantum mechanics result with implications for quantum ML and measurement-based protocols — understanding how modified measurement rules alter many-body dynamics is relevant to quantum circuit and quantum ML research.
cards.summary: Replacing the Born rule with a warped version p_b(m) ∝ ‖P_m|ψ⟩‖^(2b) introduces a probabilistic bias in repeated local measurements. For b>1, the gas freezes into clustered configurations (Maxwell's demon-like entropy extraction); for b<1, it becomes hyperuniform. Results are derived analytically for a 1D quantum gas and confirmed numerically via matrix product state simulations with projective-measurement circuits.

cards.title: Constructive Topological Expressivity Bounds for ReLU Networks via Betti Numbers of Outputs
cards.why_it_matters: For researchers studying neural network theory, this shifts expressivity analysis from decision boundaries to network outputs, providing constructive architectural bounds applicable beyond classification.
cards.summary: The authors prove that a ReLU network with a specific architecture can express spaces homotopy equivalent to wedge sums of spheres with arbitrary Betti numbers, giving upper bounds for any connected Betti-number sequence. Better bounds are achieved for product-of-spheres spaces, yielding architecture (∑d_n, 3∑d_n+2N, ∑d_n+N). A conjecture proposes a tight bound of (d, d+1, d+1) for a sphere-homeomorphic space.
